newsitem.title: CONGO: Brazzaville calm after call for talks.
newsitem.headline: Brazzaville calm after call for talks.

text.p: The Congo capital Brazzaville was calm on Monday after mediators called for talks on ending political violence that has killed hundreds of people.
Residents said the situation was about the calmest they had seen since the conflict erupted on June 5, although one witness reported a brief burst of firing around daybreak.
The national committee mediating in the conflict opposing President Pascal Lissouba and former military ruler Denis Sassou Nguesso on Sunday invited both parties to talks on Wednesday.
Neither side has indicated whether they will attend.

Committee chairman Bernard Kolelas, the city mayor, has met the two chief protagonists separately in the past. But in announcing the new talks, he did not make clear if he expected Sassou and Lissouba to attend.
Clashes broke out when government troops surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias ahead of planned July 27 elections.
Efforts to resolve the conflict have been frustrated by squabbling over who started the fighting.
However, the most contentious issue now is whether Lisouba's mandate expiring at the end of August should be extended to allow the organisation of elections, which must now be delayed.

Lissouba says the constitution provides for his mandate to be prolonged until elections can take place. Sassou says the constitution makes no such provision and that a neutral transitional authority must govern the country in the runup to elections.
President Omar Bongo of neighbouring Gabon, a son-in-law of Sassou and a friend of Lissouba, is leading a separate international mediation effort.
In 1993 political clashes killed at least 2,000 people in Brazzaville after a disputed parliamentary election.
